title: Income Tax Department User Manual on Bank Account Pre-Validation and Failure Resolution
section: Bank Pre-Validation Failures, Name Mismatch Errors, and EVC Integration
text:
Income Tax Bank Pre-Validation Failure Resolution: The Centralized Processing Center (CPC 2.0) validates bank accounts against core banking systems via automated APIs to credit tax refunds. 

Root Causes of Validation Failure: 1. Demographic Discrepancies: Legal name on PAN card does not match the account holder name registered in the bank's Core Banking Solution (CBS). 2. Unlinked PAN in CBS: PAN is not seeded or marked inactive within the bank branch database. 3. Metadata Obsolescence (IFSC Mismatch): The bank branch underwent an institutional merger (e.g. Syndicate Bank merged into Canara Bank, Allahabad Bank into Indian Bank, Andhra Bank/Corporation Bank into Union Bank of India), causing legacy IFSC codes to be decommissioned. 

Direct Resolution Steps: 1. Log in to incometax.gov.in. Navigate to 'Profile > My Bank Account'. Click the red exclamation flag next to the failed bank account to read the exact API error code. 2. Remove obsolete accounts and click 'Add Bank Account'. Enter the updated IFSC and account number. 3. Ensure your name in your bank account matches your PAN card letter-for-letter. Contact your home branch to update CBS records if necessary. 4. Pre-validate using Aadhaar OTP or Electronic Verification Code (EVC). 5. Once validated (green checkmark), toggle 'Nominated for Refund' to ON. 

Statutory TAT: Automated bank pre-validation completes within 24 to 48 hours.

title: Income Tax Portal Manual on Resolving 'Refund Unpaid' and Refund Reissue Requests
section: Resolution Workflows for Failed Tax Refunds and 'Refund Unpaid' Diagnostic States
text:
Resolving 'Refund Unpaid' and 'Returned' Diagnostic States: When a tax refund determined by CPC Bengaluru cannot clear the banking network, the e-filing portal marks the remittance status as 'Refund Unpaid' or 'Returned'. Refiling the income tax return does NOT resolve this state. 

Root Cause: NACH automated clearing house settlement failure due to invalid bank IFSC, closed account, or bank account name mismatch. 

Direct Resolution Steps: 1. Resolve underlying banking errors: Correct your bank account details in your bank's Core Banking Solution and validate the account on the e-filing portal under 'Profile > My Bank Account' with 'Nominated for Refund' enabled. 2. Initiate Refund Reissue Request: Go to 'Services > Refund Reissue > Create Refund Reissue Request'. 3. The portal displays the failed refund record. Select the record and choose the green-flagged validated bank account. 4. Complete two-factor e-verification using Aadhaar OTP, Net Banking EVC, or Digital Signature Certificate (DSC). 5. Submit the request. The CPC routes the request through automated validation checks. 

Statutory TAT & Escalation: State Bank of India (Refund Banker) dispatches the electronic refund via NACH within 7 to 10 working days of approval. If delayed past 15 days, call CPC Helpdesk Toll-Free 1800 103 0025 or raise a grievance on e-Filing Grievances.

title: Income Tax Manual on Section 119(2)(b) Condonation of Delay for Expired ITR Verification
section: Section 119(2)(b) Delay Condonation Petitions for Expired 30-Day e-Verification
text:
Section 119(2)(b) Condonation of Delay for Expired e-Verification: Statutory compliance requires that every filed Income Tax Return be e-verified or physically verified within 30 calendar days of submission. Missing this 30-day window renders the return non-est, meaning it is legally treated as if never submitted. 

Root Cause: Taxpayer missed verifying within 30 days due to genuine hardship, medical emergencies, non-receipt of OTP, or portal downtime. 

Direct Resolution via Condonation Petition: 1. Log in to the e-Filing portal (incometax.gov.in) with your PAN. 2. Navigate to 'Services > Service Request'. 3. Click 'Create Service Request' and select 'Condonation Request'. 4. Choose Request Type as 'Condonation of Delay in verification of Return' and click 'Continue'. 5. Select the relevant Assessment Year and Acknowledgement Number of the unverified return. 6. Select the reason for delay from the dropdown (e.g. medical emergency, technical difficulty, postal delay) and provide a detailed factual explanation in the remarks box. Upload supporting medical or technical documentation if applicable. 7. Submit and e-verify the service request. 

Statutory TAT: The jurisdictional tax authority (Pr. CCIT/CCIT/CIT) reviews the petition. Once condoned, the taxpayer receives an intimation email and can complete e-verification on the portal without penalty.

title: Income Tax User Manual on Responding to Section 139(9) Defective Return Notices
section: Responding to Section 139(9) Defective Return Notices and Prima Facie Adjustments
text:
Section 139(9) Defective Return Notice Rectification: The Centralized Processing Center (CPC 2.0) issues an intimation under Section 139(9) declaring an ITR defective when internal discrepancies, incomplete schedules, or tax credit mismatches (TDS vs Form 26AS/AIS) are detected during automated processing. 

CRITICAL LEGAL WARNING: The taxpayer must upload a corrected schema under the 'Defective Return' module in response to Section 139(9). Filing a revised return under Section 139(5) does NOT cure a Section 139(9) defect notice and will result in the return being declared invalid! 

Direct Resolution Steps: 1. Log in to incometax.gov.in with PAN. 2. Navigate to 'Pending Actions > e-Proceedings > Self'. 3. Locate the notice under 'Section 139(9) - Defective Return'. Download the defect memo to review specific defect codes. 4. Prepare the rectified return JSON using offline utility or online portal, ensuring you select 'In response to notice under Section 139(9)' and quote the original Acknowledgement Number. 5. In 'e-Proceedings > Defective Notice', click 'Submit Response', select 'Agree', upload the rectified JSON file, and e-verify immediately via Aadhaar OTP or DSC. 

Statutory Statutory Deadline: Strict statutory window of 15 calendar days from the date of receipt of the notice. If not rectified within 15 days, the return is declared invalid (never filed), attracting late fees under Section 234F.

title: Income Tax Department Comprehensive Guide: Individual Taxpayer ITR Filing Workflow
section: Step-by-Step e-Filing Workflow for Individual Citizens on eportal.incometax.gov.in
text:
Standard Individual Citizen ITR Filing Protocol: Resident individuals file their Income Tax Return electronically through the official e-Filing portal (eportal.incometax.gov.in). 

Pre-Filing Preparations: 1. Log in to eportal.incometax.gov.in using your PAN as User ID and your password. 2. Cross-Verify Income & Tax Credits: Navigate to 'e-File > Income Tax Returns > View Form 26AS' and 'e-File > AIS (Annual Information Statement) / TIS (Taxpayer Information Summary)'. Cross-check salary TDS, interest income, and advance tax payments against your Form 16 and bank passbooks. 3. Bank Account Validation: Ensure at least one savings bank account is pre-validated under Profile > My Bank Account for receiving tax refunds. 

Selecting the Correct ITR Form: - Form ITR-1 (Sahaj): For resident individuals having total income up to Rs 50 Lakhs from Salary/Pension, one House Property, and Other Sources (interest, dividend). Not for capital gains or business income. - Form ITR-2: For individuals/HUFs with capital gains (stocks, mutual funds, property), foreign assets/income, more than one house property, or income exceeding Rs 50 Lakhs. - Form ITR-3: For individuals having income from business or profession. - Form ITR-4 (Sugam): For resident individuals, HUFs, and firms having total income up to Rs 50 Lakhs under presumptive taxation schemes (Section 44AD, 44ADA, 44AE). 

e-Filing Steps: Go to e-File > Income Tax Returns > File Income Tax Return. Select Assessment Year (AY), choose status as 'Individual', select the appropriate ITR form, review pre-filled data, fill deductions under Chapter VI-A (80C, 80D), verify tax computation, and click 'Proceed to Validation'. 

Mandatory e-Verification within 30 Days: Under statutory CBDT rules, filing is incomplete without verification within 30 calendar days of submission. The fastest method is Instant e-Verification via Aadhaar OTP (mobile must be linked to Aadhaar), NetBanking, or Bank Account EVC. Alternatively, mail a physical signed ITR-V acknowledgement slip to 'CPC, Post Box No. 1, Electronic City Post Office, Bengaluru-560100, Karnataka' within 30 days.

title: Income Tax Department User Guide on Submitting Feedback on Annual Information Statement (AIS)
section: Submitting Online Feedback for SFT and Tax Credit Discrepancies in AIS and TIS
text:
Annual Information Statement (AIS) Feedback Submission Protocol: Taxpayers can review financial transactions reported by reporting entities (SFT filers, banks, stock depositories) and submit transaction-level feedback directly on the e-filing portal.

Direct Resolution Steps:
1. Log in to incometax.gov.in with PAN and password.
2. Navigate to 'Services > Annual Information Statement (AIS)'. Click 'Proceed' to redirect to the AIS compliance portal.
3. Open the 'AIS' tab and select the relevant Financial Year. The screen displays Part A (General Information) and Part B (TDS/TCS, SFT, Payment of Taxes, Demand/Refund, Other Information).
4. Under Part B, select the transaction category (e.g., SFT-005 for dividends, SFT-006 for interest, or securities transactions).
5. Click on the specific transaction displaying an incorrect value or duplicate entry. Click 'Feedback' on the right side of the screen.
6. Select the applicable feedback option from the dropdown:
   - 'Information is correct'
   - 'Information is not fully correct' (specify correct amount)
   - 'Information relates to other PAN/Year'
   - 'Information is duplicate / already reported'
   - 'Information is denied'
7. Submit the feedback. The system generates an Acknowledgement Receipt.

Statutory Effect & TIS Update: Upon feedback submission, the modified value is immediately reflected in the Taxpayer Information Summary (TIS) as the 'Derived Value' used for pre-filling ITR. AIS feedback is NOT a Section 139(9) defective return proceeding, does not require filing a rectified JSON schema under e-Proceedings, and does not have a 15-day defect memo deadline.
